Name: Graza Sizzle
Description: Single-origin Picual from Jaén in a squeeze bottle designed for high-heat cooking. Harvest-dated, transparent sourcing, cold-extracted.
PillarGood: Picual cultivar, Jaén province. Cold centrifugal extraction, unfiltered. Acidity stated below 0.4%. Harvest month and year printed on label. Picual has documented oxidative stability relative to other common cultivars, consistent with high-heat use.
PillarClean: Single origin: Jaén, Andalusia. Variety stated on label. Mill location disclosed. Not certified organic. No blending with other origins or varieties declared. QR code links to additional production information.
PillarFair: Sourced from a co-operative mill in Jaén. Direct-to-consumer distribution model. No third-party fair trade or equivalent certification.
PillarTrue: Heat stability claim is consistent with published oxidative stability data for Picual. Harvest date disclosure reduces reliance on best-before dating alone. No legacy phrases such as 'first cold press' used.

Name: Graza Drizzle
Description: Single-origin Arbequina from Catalonia in a drizzle-optimized bottle. Mild, fruity, harvest-dated — designed for finishing and raw applications.
PillarGood: Arbequina cultivar, Catalonia. Cold extraction. Acidity stated below 0.4%. Harvest date printed on label. Arbequina has a lower polyphenol and oxidative stability profile relative to varieties such as Picual or Koroneiki — consistent with raw use rather than high-heat applications.
PillarClean: Single origin: Catalonia, Spain. Variety stated on label. Mill location disclosed. Not certified organic. No blending across origins or varieties declared.
PillarFair: Sourced from a co-operative mill in Catalonia. Direct-to-consumer distribution model. No third-party fair trade certification.
PillarTrue: Raw/finishing positioning is consistent with Arbequina's published chemical profile. Harvest date stated. No unsupported quality descriptors.

Name: Bono Sicilia PGI EVOO
Description: EU PGI-certified Sicilian EVOO with independent certification by IRVO, the Italian government's olive oil authority. Each bottle carries a unique traceable serial number.
PillarGood: Acidity 0.2–0.4% (producer-reported). Native Sicilian cultivars. Harvest year stated on label under the 'Raccolto' designation.
PillarClean: EU PGI certification requires olives to be grown, pressed, and bottled within Sicily. Compliance is verified by IRVO (Istituto Regionale Vitivinicolo), operating under the Italian Ministry of Agriculture. Each bottle carries a unique serial number traceable through IRVO records.
PillarFair: Co-operative structure with member growers within the PGI zone. Revenue distribution to member growers is a structural feature of co-operative models. No additional fair trade certification.
PillarTrue: PGI geographic origin is independently certified, not self-declared. Vintage year disclosure is required under PGI rules. PGI requires production and bottling within the designated zone, which distinguishes this product from non-PGI Italian-labelled oils that may source olives from multiple countries.

Name: Kirkland Signature EVOO
Description: Costco's house-label EVOO. Independently tested and confirmed to meet EVOO grade standards. Italian blend without specific regional disclosure.
PillarGood: Independent laboratory testing (including UC Davis and Consumer Reports analyses) has confirmed EVOO grade compliance. Mild sensory profile consistent with a neutral blend. Harvest date not consistently printed; freshness relative to pressing date cannot be determined from label alone.
PillarClean: Labeled as Italian blend. No specific regional or varietal disclosure. No PDO or DOP certification. Meets IOC-defined EVOO grade criteria based on independent testing.
PillarFair: Private label product manufactured at high volume. Supply chain details for grower compensation are not publicly disclosed. No fair trade or co-operative certification.
PillarTrue: No single-origin or estate claims made. 'Italian' designation reflects bottling location under EU labelling regulations — olives may originate from multiple countries. This is not disclosed on label but is consistent with current EU rules.

Name: Terra Delyssa Organic EVOO
Description: Organic Tunisian EVOO with blockchain QR-code traceability. Chemlali and Chetoui cultivars pressed within 4 hours of harvest. USDA Organic, Ecocert, and NAOOA certified.
PillarGood: Time from harvest to pressing stated as under 4 hours. Cold-pressed. Harvest date accessible via QR code linked to IBM Food Trust blockchain records. Chemlali and Chetoui cultivars.
PillarClean: USDA Organic and Ecocert certified. QR code links to blockchain provenance data (IBM Food Trust) recording harvest date, location, and production timeline. Non-GMO Project Verified. Kosher certified.
PillarFair: Vertically integrated — sourcing from company-owned orchards. No third-party fair trade certification.
PillarTrue: Tunisia stated as country of origin. 'First cold press' appears on some products — this is legacy phrasing; centrifugal extraction at controlled temperature is the actual method used in modern facilities. Blockchain records allow the stated origin and timing to be independently verified by the consumer.

Name: Kosterina Original EVOO
Description: Early-harvest Koroneiki EVOO from southern Greece. Per-batch independent polyphenol testing published on website. USDA Organic certified.
PillarGood: Koroneiki cultivar, Peloponnese. Early harvest. Per-batch polyphenol results published by producer; values reported above 500 mg/kg in available test data. USDA Organic certified.
PillarClean: Peloponnese origin stated. USDA Organic certified. Third-party laboratory polyphenol test results published per harvest batch. Early harvest designation is supported by published chemical data.
PillarFair: Direct-to-consumer distribution. Producer states intent to support family olive growers in Greece. No third-party fair trade or equivalent certification.
PillarTrue: Polyphenol values are documented per batch with published laboratory reports. 'Early harvest' designation is supported by chemical data, not asserted without evidence. Health-related references cite IOC-recognised research on olive oil phenolic compounds.

Name: Cobram Estate Classic EVOO
Description: Australian EVOO producer. Southern hemisphere harvest (May–June) delivers fresh oil to Northern Hemisphere markets while Mediterranean stocks age. AOCA certified, harvest-dated.
PillarGood: Australian harvest in May–June. AOCA certified. Stated product parameters: FFA below 0.3%, peroxide value below 8 meq/kg, polyphenols above 250 mg/kg. Harvest date printed on label.
PillarClean: Olives grown, milled, and bottled in Victoria, Australia. AOCA certification requires independent grade verification. One product line uses the name 'California Select' — the oil is Australian; country of origin (Australia) is stated in fine print.
PillarFair: Large-scale vertically integrated operation. Labor subject to Australian workplace legislation. No fair trade or co-operative certification.
PillarTrue: 'California Select' is a quality tier designation, not a geographic origin claim. Country of origin (Australia) is disclosed on label in fine print. Harvest date and AOCA certification status are stated accurately.

Name: McEvoy Ranch Organic EVOO
Description: 550-acre certified organic estate in Marin County. Tuscan varietal blend harvested November–December. COOC certified, USDA Organic, harvest date on label.
PillarGood: Tuscan varietal blend (Frantoio, Leccino, Moraiolo) from estate-grown trees. Harvested annually in November–December. COOC certified. Harvest date printed on each bottle.
PillarClean: Single estate: Petaluma, Marin County, California. USDA Organic and COOC certified. All olives grown, harvested, and milled on the estate. No external sourcing declared.
PillarFair: Estate operation with direct employment. Small-batch production. No third-party fair trade certification.
PillarTrue: 'Tuscan' refers to varietal lineage (Frantoio, Leccino, Moraiolo), not Italian geographic origin — this distinction is reflected in labelling. COOC certification independently verifies grade claims. No legacy marketing phrases used.

Name: Equal Exchange Organic EVOO
Description: Worker-owned co-operative sourcing fair trade organic EVOO from Palestinian smallholder farmers in the West Bank.
PillarGood: Rumi cultivar, a native Palestinian variety. USDA Organic certified. Harvest date disclosed on label.
PillarClean: USDA Organic and Fair Trade certified. Single origin: West Bank, Palestine. Sourced through named farmer co-operatives. Supply chain documented as a requirement of fair trade certification.
PillarFair: Equal Exchange is itself a worker-owned co-operative. Palestinian farmer partners receive fair trade premiums; premium allocation is documented in published annual reports, covering community infrastructure and co-operative development.
PillarTrue: Country of origin (Palestine) stated explicitly on label. Fair trade and organic certifications are third-party verified. No regional umbrella language used in place of specific origin.

Name: Canaan Fair Trade Organic EVOO
Description: Palestinian co-operative working with approximately 2,500 farmers across 55 co-operatives. Regenerative Organic Certified as of 2024, covering approximately 20,000 acres.
PillarGood: Rumi and Nabali cultivars, native Palestinian varieties. Organic farming without synthetic inputs. Harvest date disclosed.
PillarClean: USDA Organic certified. Fair Trade certified (IMO). Regenerative Organic Certified (ROC) as of 2024, requiring third-party verification of soil health, animal welfare, and social fairness criteria. Sourcing documented across 52 communities and 55 co-operatives.
PillarFair: Founded by agronomist Nasser Abufarha. Established in 2004. Published annual reports document fair trade premium allocation over a 20-year period, including women's co-operative programs and rural infrastructure projects.
PillarTrue: Palestinian origin stated explicitly in labelling. Fair trade and Regenerative Organic certifications are independently verified. No geographic softening used in place of country of origin.

Name: Citizens of Soil EVOO
Description: Curated single-estate EVOOs from small farms in Croatia. Subscription model with seasonal releases.
PillarGood: Each release sourced from a named single estate. Harvest date disclosed per release. Variety specified per bottle. Availability tied to actual seasonal harvest cycles.
PillarClean: Each oil sourced from named farms with disclosed locations. No blending across origins. Farming practices vary by producer; some certified regenerative or biodynamic, others in documented transition.
PillarFair: Subscription model provides predictable demand for small producers without established export distribution. Sourcing relationships with individual producers are documented on product pages.
PillarTrue: Citizens of Soil operates as a curator and buyer, not a producer — this is stated in product descriptions. Each oil is labeled by specific estate and harvest year. Country of origin (Croatia) is stated without regional umbrella language.

Name: Brightland Alive EVOO
Description: California EVOO from Arbosana and Arbequina olives. Cold-pressed within 90 minutes of harvest. COOC certified.
PillarGood: Heirloom Arbosana and Arbequina blend. Cold-pressed, stated within 90 minutes of harvest. COOC certified — grade verified by independent testing. Nitrogen-flushed UV-protective glass. Harvest date printed on label.
PillarClean: California origin, San Joaquin Valley. COOC certified. Harvest date disclosed. Not certified organic. UV-protective glass bottle used.
PillarFair: Direct-to-consumer model. Works with family farms in the San Joaquin Valley. No third-party fair trade certification. Labor subject to California agricultural legislation.
PillarTrue: COOC certification independently verifies grade claims. No legacy phrases used. Brand materials cite documented research on olive oil adulteration as context for sourcing approach.

Name: Ayvaco EVOO
Description: Single-origin EVOO from a family farm in the Ayvalık region. Direct-to-consumer, harvest-dated.
PillarGood: Ayvalık cultivar, a native Turkish variety. Harvest date disclosed. Direct-from-farm distribution reduces time in supply chain.
PillarClean: Single farm, Ayvalık region, Turkey. Direct-to-consumer. No organic certification confirmed in available product information.
PillarFair: Single family farm, direct-to-consumer. No intermediary distribution declared.
PillarTrue: 'First cold press' is stated — this is legacy phrasing without current regulatory meaning under modern centrifugal extraction. Otherwise, labelling is consistent with stated single-farm sourcing and harvest date.

Name: Papa Vince EVOO
Description: Single-estate Nocellara del Belice from Santa Ninfa, Sicily. Family operation since 1935, unfiltered and unblended. Lot traceability to grove and harvest date.
PillarGood: Nocellara del Belice cultivar. Unfiltered. Harvest lot number and date printed on label. No synthetic pesticides or herbicides declared.
PillarClean: Single estate, Santa Ninfa, Sicily. All stages (cultivation, harvest, pressing) conducted at the same estate. Lot traceability to grove and harvest period. Direct shipping from Sicily.
PillarFair: Family estate with stated continuous operation since 1935. Direct-to-consumer, no distributor intermediary declared.
PillarTrue: 'Unblended' and 'unfiltered' claims are consistent with single-estate production. Lot number enables traceability. 'First cold press' appears in marketing — legacy phrasing; current method is cold centrifugal extraction.

Name: Masseria Estate Organic EVOO
Description: USDA Organic certified single-origin Sicilian EVOO. Nocellara Etnea cultivar grown in volcanic soil near Mt. Etna.
PillarGood: Nocellara Etnea cultivar, Mt. Etna zone. USDA Organic certified. Small-batch production. Early harvest.
PillarClean: USDA Organic certified. Single origin: Nocellara Etnea cultivar, Mt. Etna zone, Sicily. Direct-to-consumer. Cultivar and growing zone disclosed.
PillarFair: Small estate, direct-to-consumer. No third-party fair trade certification.
PillarTrue: Nocellara Etnea is a named native Sicilian cultivar. USDA Organic certification is federally verified. Mt. Etna growing zone designation is geographically accurate to the stated production area.

Name: FIORE Artisan Olive Oils
Origin: Various — seasonal releases from Spain, Italy, Chile, New Zealand, California
Description: Seasonal curation sourcing oils from small producers as each hemisphere's harvest completes. Oils are released as limited runs and change each season.
PillarGood: Each release single-origin and variety-specific. Harvest date disclosed per release. Oils are sourced at the point of harvest completion in each producing region.
PillarClean: Each release identifies the specific producing farm, harvest date, and origin. No blending across origins. Certification status varies by producer and is specified per release.
PillarFair: Long-term sourcing relationships with individual small producers. Seasonal purchasing provides consistent demand for producers without established US distribution.
PillarTrue: FIORE operates as a buyer and curator, not a producer — this is stated in product descriptions. Country and region of origin stated per bottle. Seasonal inventory rotation is disclosed.

Name: California Olive Ranch Classic EVOO
Origin: California, USA (primary) + international blend components in some lines
Description: Largest domestic US olive oil producer. COOC certified, harvest-dated, Non-GMO Project Verified.
PillarGood: COOC certified — grade verified by independent testing. Harvest date printed on label. Consistent performance in independent quality assessments.
PillarClean: COOC certified. Harvest date disclosed. Non-GMO Project Verified. Two distinct product lines: '100% California' (fully domestic) and 'Global Blend' (California oil combined with international sources). The distinction is stated on label.
PillarFair: Large-scale domestic producer. Supply chain details for international blend components are not publicly disclosed. No fair trade or co-operative certification.
PillarTrue: 'California' branding on the domestic line is accurate and COOC-verified. 'Global Blend' labelling is transparent about non-California sourcing. Harvest date stated. No misleading country-of-origin claims made.
